title: The runtime resolves the `@mandate` records that govern an actor, its default actor and a mode's refusal profile
summary: @inventarch/runtime exports governingMandates(handle, within, {actor?, path?, workspace?}), defaultActor(handle, within, workspace) and profileRefusal(mandates, mode, words?) from the package root and the @inventarch/runtime/internal/mandate-modes subpath, with the GoverningOptions, GoverningMandate, DefaultActor, ProfileMandate and ProfileVerdict types, and registers IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR in RUNTIME_CODES and MANDATE_CODES. governingMandates and defaultActor read through the scope token alone, profileRefusal reads nothing, and none needs a clean workspace: one with admission errors resolves what admission admitted, except that while an authored `@mandate` fails admission, or a record an admitted mandate or workspace depends on does, governingMandates and defaultActor fail closed with IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID (described in the mandate-admission note). A record at runtime placement is never read, only authored (band 100) `@mandate` records govern, and only those of the workspace's closure as position reads it (without a workspace, that of the workspace position seats the path in, else the repository's own), so a mandate under another workspace's declared root never governs or names a participant there. governingMandates returns the governing mandates by identity, each with its moves, covers and excluded words (present when the record states the key) and its participant and scope references resolved to identities: with workspace or path, those whose authority.scope names the workspace or whose authority.covers selects the path, either sufficing, and one that states neither key with a value (a declared empty list locates nothing, so it never lifts a restriction) wherever its participant acts (with actor, only when that participant is the actor); with neither, every one. An actor drops no governing mandate: each then carries binds, true when its participant is that `@agent` or it names none. defaultActor names the `@agent` a mandate-gated command acts as: the workspace's composition.steward when it is an authored (band 100) `@agent` (an installed steward names none, as if none were stated), else the one authored participant its scoped mandates name, and lists in actors the identities a command may be told to act as, the participants and the authored steward; with several participants and no authored steward it names none and returns IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR, whose next command is ia position --seat <workspace> --shape governance, and with none it returns only a reason. profileRefusal returns {refusal?, notice?}: it leaves out a mandate that binds another participant and returns IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR when every governing mandate does, or when the rest bind several participants, whose moves it never pools; otherwise a mode is allowed when any remaining mandate grants its move (lists it or declares no moves), else IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-MOVE, and, when words are given, a word any of them excludes is IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-WORD; each refusal names ia position --seat <mandate> --shape governance; with no governing mandate nothing is restricted and the notice says so. A missing token, an actor or workspace that is not an admitted record of its word, an unknown mode, or a governing mandate whose authority mandateAuthorityOf refuses is IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID. Limits: @inventarch/cli's mandate profile (its gated commands, defaultActor included) and the edit guard (evaluateMandateGuard, which @inventarch/steward-hook's `--hook` mode calls for each edit an authored `@hook` selects) consult them, and @inventarch/workspace-runtime's agent-profile generation reads governingMandates for a profile that names no mandate; no Door operation does; mandateRefusal still names ia inspect <mandate> --edges both; a mandate grants no host permission; the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2, every ia scope form, position, body(K) and the packet renderer are unchanged.
